newsitem.title: CHINA: China says grain harvest to boost stocks.
newsitem.headline: China says grain harvest to boost stocks.

text.p: Much of China's projected record grain harvest in 1996 will be used to boost low stocks, an official of the Ministry of Agriculture said.
"The grain harvest this year will be mainly used to build up stocks held by farmers themselves," said the official, who declined to be identified by name.
The remarks were made on Wednesday but on condition they be withheld from publication until Thursday.

He told reporters that grain inventories held by farmers declined sharply over the past several years because of increases in state grain purchase prices. That encouraged farmers to sell grain to the state.
He declined to reveal the current level of state grain reserves.
The State Statistical Bureau said on Wednesday that China's grain harvest this year would reach a record 480 million tonnes.
China still had no official plan to resume full-scale corn exports despite this year's encouraging corn harvest in the northeast, the key producing areas, the official said.
Much of the corn harvested in the northeast this year would be allocated to southern provinces to offset their shortages, he said without giving further details.
China banned corn exports in 1994 to curb rising domestic prices. It still exported 110,000 tonnes last year -- but the shipments were considered special cases, as were offshore sales this year.
China exported 150,000 tonnes of corn in the first nine months of 1996, up 41.3 percent from the year-ago period, the Futures Herald newspaper has said, quoting customs figures.
Exports in September alone were 30,000 tonnes, it said.
China exported 8.74 million tonnes of corn in 1994.
